messages.subject: Update to package v1.5.0
messages.body_plain:
Hello, I have made an update to v1.5.0. You can see the changes at the NEWS.md file <https://github.com/cwatson/brainGraph/commit/3cee2be0a265844b164c49d105da45faab4c357c?short_path=8312ad0#diff-8312ad0561ef661716b48d09478362f3>.

Most of the changes are regarding "boot_global": there are a couple new arguments, and it now works properly for weighted graphs.

For "set_brainGraph_attr", there is a new argument, "xfm.type". This represents the method you would like to transform edge weights (necessary for distance-based metrics, such as characteristic path length). The default value is the reciprocal, which was the only possibility in previous versions. You may also choose the negative natural logarithm, or "1 - w" (subtract each edge weight from 1). The latter may be desirable if your edge weights are between 0 and 1.

Please let me know if you have any errors when using the new version.
Chris

messages.subject: Update to v1.6.0
messages.body_plain:
Hello, I have updated the package to v1.6.0. The only change here is to "brainGraph_init"; you can now specify a custom atlas by setting
atlas="custom"

in the function call, and specifying the name of your atlas by
custom.atlas="myAtlas"

(substituting "myAtlas" for the correct name). The full changes can be seen at the NEWS.md file <https://github.com/cwatson/brainGraph/commit/915d8750170a1c76c8fcad336ab626b8f754d63f?short_path=8312ad0#diff-8312ad0561ef661716b48d09478362f3>.

Chris

Hi Jonathan,

I describe the usage in Chapter 7 of my User Guide (you can download here if you haven't seen it yet: https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/s/wmupawb39bcdho3/brainGraph_UserGuide.pdf

Briefly,
* g.list: a list of lists of graphs. There should be 3 "levels" to the list, for (in order): group, threshold, subject
* thresholds: the numeric vector of thresholds applied to the raw connectivity matrices. I am unfamiliar with PET so I am not sure what this would be for your purposes. The actual values of this vector aren't important for any computations, so if you wanted, you could set it equal to 1:k (where k is the number of thresholds)
* N: the number of permutations (default = 500)
* perms: a "permute" object, which is essentially a matrix of the permutation order for all 1:N (default = NULL; i.e., you don't have to input anything for this, if you don't want to)
* alpha: the significance level (default = 0.05)

The remaining arguments are required for the calls to "brainGraph_GLM", and include:
* covars: a "data.table" of your covariates; this must have a column titled "Study.ID"
* measure: the graph measure you are interested in testing. If it happens to be, e.g., modularity, you would specify "mod"
* con.vec: an integer vector specifying your contrast of interest
* alt: the alternative hypothesis (default: two.sided)

There are others that are specific to building the design matrix, such as:
* coding (dummy, effects, or cell.means)
* mean.center (TRUE or FALSE)
* binarize (if you want to convert a factor into an integer vector)
* int (whether you want to include an interaction term)

Chapter 7 describes everything in great detail, but if there is anything I haven't explained well, please feel free to ask more questions.

Chris

Hi Ozgun et al., I have figured out the problem.

Since v1.0.0, I combined "permute.group" and "permute.group.auc". This requires a change to the structure of custom functions. I forgot to update the User Guide accordingly. For EV and closeness centralities, the code would be:

evcent.diffs.perm <- function(g, densities) {
  meas.list <- lapply(g, function(x) t(sapply(x, function(y) centr_eigen(y)$vector)))
  my.diff <- sapply(seq_along(V(g[[1]][[1]])), function(x)
      brainGraph:::auc_diff(densities, cbind(meas.list[[1]][, x], meas.list[[2]][, x])))
  tmp <- as.data.table(t(my.diff))
  setnames(tmp, 1:ncol(tmp), V(g[[1]][[1]])$name)
  return(tmp)
}

For closeness, replace "centr_eigen(y)$vector" with "centr_clo(y)$res" in the function (and be sure to change the function name, accordingly).

In the future I will likely make this a much easier process. And probably I will add these 2 measures to the hard-coded version, so then you can just type measure="ev.cent", for example.

Chris
